Pick a rule again from a tuning table, at another width of the region

Source: R/tune_repick.R
knw_tune_repick.Rd

knw_tune_score() keeps every rule whose held-out score is within one standard error of the best (the region) and picks the region rule with the fewest departures from default, ties to the lower score, moving off a pick whose exception distance is under d_floor. One standard error is a parsimony rule of thumb fixed before the run, not a boundary of noise; this replays the same pick from the saved table at any multiple of the standard error, so a reader can see which picks hold under a stricter bar (1.96).

Usage

knw_tune_repick(tune, se_mult = 1, d_floor = 200, start = c("default", "flow"))

Arguments

tune

a tuning table as knw_tune_score() returns it and scripts/0320 saves it (<sp>_<stage>_tune.csv), in grid order: rule, departures, exc_d, converged, dev_heldout, ddev_best and se_diff.

se_mult

numeric(1) the region's width in standard errors.

d_floor

numeric(1) the shortest exception distance (m) a recommended rule may carry, as in knw_tune_score().

start

"default" counts departures from link's default (the table's departures); "flow" from its flow version (departures_flow, knw_tune_grid(); #80), and is refused on a table without that column or whose species has no flow start.

Value

The recommended row of tune (one row), with n_region, the number of rules in the region at se_mult.

Details

The region is converged & ddev_best <= se_mult * se_diff, which at se_mult = 1 is the table's own in_region, so the pick at 1 is the table's recommended rule.

Examples

tune <- data.frame(
  rule = c("width>=1.5|g<=0.0549|none", "mad>=0.75|g<=0.09|Q3@D1000", "mad>=0.75|g<=0.0549|none"),
  departures = c(0L, 3L, 1L), exc_d = c(NA, 1000, NA), converged = TRUE,
  dev_heldout = c(1150, 1000, 1040), ddev_best = c(150, 0, 40), se_diff = c(60, 0, 25)
)
knw_tune_repick(tune)$rule              # 1 SE: only the best rule is close enough
#> [1] "mad>=0.75|g<=0.09|Q3@D1000"
knw_tune_repick(tune, se_mult = 1.96)$rule  # 1.96 SE: the one-departure rule joins, and is picked
#> [1] "mad>=0.75|g<=0.0549|none"
